Works inside photos/ and uses grep and sed to test and build the new name.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd photos
for f in *; do
  [[ -f $f ]] || continue
  if printf '%s\n' "$f" | grep -Eq '^IMG_[0-9]{8}_[0-9]{6}\.jpg$'; then
    new=$(printf '%s\n' "$f" | sed -E 's/^IMG_([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})_([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})\.jpg$/\1-\2-\3_\4-\5-\6.jpg/')
    mv -- "$f" "$new"
  fi
done

import csv
import json
from decimal import Decimal

totals = {}
with open("expenses.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    for row in csv.DictReader(fh):
        name = row["category"]
        totals[name] = totals.get(name, Decimal("0")) + Decimal(row["amount"])

with open("by_category.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    writer = csv.writer(fh)
    writer.writerow(["category", "total"])
    for name, value in sorted(totals.items()):
        writer.writerow([name, "%.2f" % value])

grand = sum(totals.values(), Decimal("0")).quantize(Decimal("0.01"))
with open("summary.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    json.dump({"categories": len(totals), "grand_total": float(grand)}, fh)
